title: Who Keeps Knocking?
summary: Someone is hammering DotTech's login page. Count the attempts and unmask the attacker.
briefing:
DotTech's customer website, dottech-web, was slow all night. The security team suspects a **brute-force attack**: someone trying password after password on the login page.

Every visit to the website is written to `/var/log/nginx/access.log` – one line per request, starting with the visitor's IP address. A failed login gets the status code `401`. The log has 2,400 lines, so counting by hand is not an option.

DotTech also runs a **honeypot**, a trap that records what attackers do. It keeps one file per attacker in `/srv/honeypot/sessions/`, named after their IP address. That folder can't be listed – you need the exact IP of the worst offender to open their file.
objective: Find the IP address with the most failed logins (status 401), then open its file in /srv/honeypot/sessions.
debrief:
Great counting! `cut` picked out the IP addresses, `sort` put identical ones next to each other, `uniq -c` counted them and `sort -n` put the biggest number last.

This pipeline answers "who did this the most?" for almost any log in seconds – security analysts use it all the time. Did you notice that the busiest visitor, `10.0.0.5`, was innocent? It is DotTech's own health check. Filtering for `401` first made all the difference.

You also met a folder you could pass through but not list (`rwx--x--x`). Without read permission you can't see what is inside, but with execute permission you can still open a file – if you know its exact name.

The lesson for DotTech: limit how many login attempts one IP address may make, and block addresses that keep failing.
hints: In a brute-force attack, the attacker fails to log in again and again – so their IP address appears in **lots** of failed logins. Don't read the log: count failed logins per IP address. Careful, the busiest visitor is not necessarily the attacker.
Build a pipeline step by step: `grep 401` keeps only the failed logins, `cut -d' ' -f1` keeps only the IP address, `sort | uniq -c` counts each address and `sort -n | tail -n 3` shows the top three.
Run `grep 401 /var/log/nginx/access.log | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -n | tail -n 1`. The winner is `203.0.113.77`, so open `cat /srv/honeypot/sessions/203.0.113.77.log`.

lines: The login page of dottech-web was hit thousands of times last night.
